solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

indicators.note: pants is British slang for rubbish, so the letters before it are treated as a rubbishy mess to be rearranged

blocks.note: the ten letters of these two words, taken as written

explanation.surface: A boss's grubby underwear, or a boss making a mess of someone's trousers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Head' looks like a noun paired with 'man', but it is a verb: to head something is to run it. Pants is British slang for rubbish.
explanation.definitionFit: To head an organisation is to run or manage it, which is what one does when one administers it.

indicators.note: cutting a word in half keeps only one half, so the second half of the word is lopped off

blocks.note: as can mean since, as in 'as it was raining'
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone has been drinking since before closing time and is now half-cut, British slang for tipsy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Half-cut' reads as tipsy, which suits a drinker, but here it cuts the word time in half.
explanation.definitionFit: Asti is a sparkling Italian wine from Piedmont, so it is a kind of alcoholic beverage.

indicators.note: something disordered has been thrown out of its proper sequence, so the letters need rearranging

blocks.note: the nine letters of these two words, taken as written

explanation.surface: A kingdom in the worst possible state of chaos.
explanation.definitionFit: A maelstrom is a violent whirlpool, and figuratively a scene of turbulent confusion and chaos.

indicators.note: clothing something means wrapping round it, so one piece is dressed around another

blocks.note: N is the standard abbreviation for new
an air is a look or manner, as in 'an air of confidence'
D is the standard abbreviation for daughter

explanation.surface: A fashion makeover, the New Look, covering a girl's backside.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's stands for 'is', linking wordplay to definition. The New Look was Dior's famous 1947 fashion line, which the surface plays on.
explanation.definitionFit: The nadir is the lowest point of anything, so it is the very bottom of a situation.

indicators.note: losing something means it goes missing, so a letter is dropped from the word

blocks.note: marines are one example of fighting troops, hence 'possibly'
a unit is one, written as the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: Someone signs up with the Marines but may lose their military unit.
explanation.walkthrough: Unit is the number one, shown as I; take that out of the troops.
explanation.definitionFit: To solder is to fuse metal pieces with molten alloy, so it fastens or connects things together.

indicators.note: securing means holding fast inside, so the opening words hold the solution within them

blocks.note: the letters run across the end of the first word and the start of the second

explanation.surface: A deal has been made that locks in a further deal.
explanation.walkthrough: The same word, agreement, appears twice: the first holds the letters, the last is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: An entente is a friendly understanding between nations, as in the Entente Cordiale between Britain and France.

clue.text: Strong beer, holding opener of bottle

indicators.note: holding means keeping inside, so one piece sits within the other
the opener of a word is its very first letter

blocks.note: ale is a type of beer
the first letter of bottle

explanation.surface: A potent beer being held in by its bottle opener.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Strong beer' looks like one phrase, but strong is the definition on its own.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone strong is capable and competent, which is one meaning of able, as in able-bodied.

indicators.note: taking something in means absorbing it, so one piece goes inside another
ultimately points to the final letter of the word before it

blocks.note: a pulse is an edible seed such as a bean or lentil
the last letter of drug

explanation.surface: A heartbeat kicked in after someone took a drug.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pulse' suggests a heartbeat, but here it is the vegetable sense: a bean.
explanation.definitionFit: Began is the past tense of begin, so it means commenced or set off, just as started does.

clue.text: Some penchant, in general, is attractive

indicators.note: some means only a portion, so a stretch of the following words is taken

blocks.note: the letters run from inside the first word through to the start of the last

explanation.surface: Having a bit of a liking for things in general is an appealing trait.
explanation.definitionFit: Something enchanting charms and delights, which is what makes a person or thing appealing.

clue.text: Greek god later takes over temple

indicators.note: taking something on board means it ends up inside, so one piece is held by another

blocks.note: Pan is the Greek god of the wild and of shepherds
then means at a later time
O is the cricket abbreviation for an over

explanation.surface: A Greek god later moves into a temple.
explanation.walkthrough: Over is O, as in cricket scorecards. The Greek setting of the surface is apt, since the original Pantheon honoured all the gods.
explanation.definitionFit: The Pantheon in Rome is a temple to all the gods, and a pantheon is any such sacred building.

clue.text: Passed water following tributary’s first river

indicators.note: first points to the opening letter of the word before it
following means coming after, so the piece named before this word is placed second

blocks.note: the first letter of tributary
to wee is to urinate, so passed water is weed

explanation.surface: A stream flowing into a river after a tributary joins it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Passed water' sounds like flowing, but it is the colloquial verb wee in the past tense, placed after the T.
explanation.definitionFit: The Tweed is a river in the Scottish Borders, part of it forming the boundary with England.

indicators.note: an explosion scatters things everywhere, so the letters are blown apart and reassembled

blocks.note: the nine letters of these two words, taken as written

explanation.surface: A large explosive charge has been ignited and is about to go off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heavy charge' reads as a big blast, but heavy is the definition, in its sluggish sense.
explanation.definitionFit: Heavy can describe feeling drowsy and slow, as with heavy eyelids, which is a lethargic state.

blocks.note: a surge is a sudden increase
a machine that is on is working

explanation.surface: A busy GP faces a rise in patients while on duty.
explanation.definitionFit: A surgeon is a medical practitioner who performs operations, so is one kind of doctor.

blocks.note: ton is an old word for fashion or style, as in 'the ton' of high society
GA is the US postal abbreviation for Georgia

explanation.surface: The US state of Georgia lags behind the latest trends.
explanation.walkthrough: 'State of Georgia' wants to be read as one phrase about the US state, but state is the definition and Georgia only gives its abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: Tonga is a Pacific island kingdom, an independent sovereign country and so a nation-state.

clue.text: Cutting line in a hospital department

indicators.note: in places one piece inside the others, which surround it

blocks.note: taken as written
ENT is the ear, nose and throat department
a string is a line or cord

explanation.surface: A queue snaking through one section of a hospital.
explanation.walkthrough: ENT, ear nose and throat, is the hospital department crosswords use most.
explanation.definitionFit: A cutting remark is sharp and biting, and astringent likewise describes harsh, caustic criticism.

indicators.note: overwhelming something means engulfing it, so one piece swallows another

blocks.note: spite is animosity, and the 's adds the S
R is short for regina, Latin for queen

explanation.surface: Bad feeling overwhelms a fairy queen among her subjects.
explanation.definitionFit: Sprites are elves or other small supernatural creatures of folklore, much like the little people.

clue.text: Petty theft finally followed by sacking

indicators.note: finally points to the closing letter of the word before it

blocks.note: the last letter of theft
rifling is ransacking, searching through and plundering

explanation.surface: Petty theft followed by dismissal from a job.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Petty theft' reads as one phrase, and sacking as being fired; both mislead.
explanation.definitionFit: Petty means small and unimportant, which is exactly what something trifling is.

blocks.note: first meaning: fire was one of the four classical basic substances
second meaning: the heating coil inside a kettle or immersion heater

explanation.surface: Fire, water and heat: the clue seems to be about the forces of nature.
explanation.walkthrough: The four classical elements were earth, air, fire and water, so 'water' tempts one to read it as another; here it goes with heater.
explanation.definitionFit: Ancient philosophy called fire a basic constituent, and a heating coil in an appliance is also given this name.

indicators.note: turning things over churns them up, so the letters come out in a new order

blocks.note: the heart of sweet is its middle letter, a crossword staple for a lover
the letters of these two words, taken as written

explanation.surface: A lover sneaks in by turning a key in the lock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sweetheart' looks like a lover but splits into sweet and heart, the middle letter of sweet.
explanation.definitionFit: Key as an adjective means crucial or vital, as in a key point, so it is the same as essential.

blocks.note: rum is a spirit distilled from sugar cane
M is the abbreviation for medium, as on clothes labels
i.e. (id est) means that is, or specifically
R is the abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: A spiritualist medium, a total stranger, gets the message exactly right.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spirit medium' reads as a psychic, but it is two separate pieces. Rum is British slang for odd.
explanation.definitionFit: Rum in informal British usage means odd or peculiar, so its comparative means more odd, or stranger.

clue.text: English love sailor going up rope

indicators.note: in a down clue, going up means reading the letters from bottom to top

blocks.note: E is the abbreviation for English
love is a score of nothing in tennis, so nil
a tar is a sailor

explanation.surface: A sailor beloved of an Englishman climbs the rigging.
explanation.walkthrough: A ratline is one of the small rope rungs sailors climb up the shrouds, so the surface picture is apt.
explanation.definitionFit: Ratlines are the short horizontal cords across a ship's shrouds, forming a ladder, so each is a piece of rope.

clue.text: Live with zero lapse reflecting blessing

indicators.note: a reflection shows things mirror-image, so the letters run in the opposite direction

blocks.note: to be is to exist or live
no means none, a zero amount
a sin is a moral lapse

explanation.surface: Living a blameless life with not one slip is something to reflect on.
explanation.walkthrough: Zero lapse is 'no sin', and that pair is turned round after BE.
explanation.definitionFit: A benison is an old literary word for a benediction, the opposite of a malison or curse.

blocks.note: a bug is an insect
a bear is an animal

explanation.surface: A bug crawling on a bear irritates it.
explanation.definitionFit: A bugbear is a persistent source of irritation or a pet hate, so it is a cause of annoyance.

blocks.note: NE is the compass abbreviation for north-east
china is Cockney rhyming slang for mate (china plate), so a pal

explanation.surface: A question about a republic in north-eastern China.
explanation.walkthrough: The capital C and question mark make China look like the country, and the answer does border it; but china is Cockney rhyming slang, china plate meaning mate.
explanation.definitionFit: Nepal became a federal republic in 2008 when its monarchy was abolished, so it is a republic in the Himalayas.

clue.text: Press addressing, perhaps, Express readers, initially

indicators.note: initially points to the opening letters of the preceding words

blocks.note: the first letters of these five words

explanation.surface: A newspaper speaking to readers of the Daily Express.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue does both jobs: the initials spell the word, and the clue as a whole describes it.
explanation.definitionFit: The Express is a British newspaper, so a paper is the press that might address its readership.

indicators.note: reportedly means as said by others, so the word is judged by how it sounds

blocks.note: a titan is a giant, a person of great size or importance

explanation.surface: A heavyweight boxer seizes up with a muscle spasm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cramp' looks like a noun for the boxer's spasm, but it is a verb: to cramp is to restrict.
explanation.definitionFit: To cramp is to confine or restrict, and to tighten something constrains it in the same way.

clue.text: President is behind after Democrat’s back

indicators.note: the back of a word is its final letter
after means coming later, so the piece named first in the clue goes second

blocks.note: the last letter of Democrat
a rump is a behind, the backside

explanation.surface: A Republican president trails behind a Democrat.
explanation.definitionFit: Donald Trump served as the 45th and 47th President of the United States.

indicators.note: embracing means hugging round, so one piece wraps around another

blocks.note: the man's can be read as he's, he is
Romeo is R in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Her husband is cuddling a would-be lover.
explanation.walkthrough: Romeo suggests a lover, fitting the lady, but it only supplies R.
explanation.definitionFit: The lady's, as in 'the bag is the lady's', means belonging to her, which is the possessive pronoun for a woman.

blocks.note: an ex is a former partner
pensive means deep in thought, brooding

explanation.surface: A beloved ex-partner who is moody and broody.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dear' looks like a term of endearment for the ex, but it means costly.
explanation.definitionFit: Dear in British usage means costing a lot of money, so it is a synonym of pricey.

clue.text: Couple in posh evening picked up

indicators.note: to pick something up is to hear it, so the word is chosen by its sound

blocks.note: U means upper-class, from 1950s talk of U and non-U usage
the evening is night time

explanation.surface: A pair of people out on a smart night on the town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Couple' looks like a noun for a pair, but it is the verb to join.
explanation.definitionFit: To couple two things is to link or join them together, which is what bringing them into one does.

indicators.note: occasionally means every so often, so only every other letter is kept

blocks.note: the first, third, fifth and seventh letters

explanation.surface: A Conservative is now and then too dull and colourless.
explanation.definitionFit: A Tory is a member of Britain's Conservative Party, the traditional nickname for the party.

clue.text: City of Rome spoilt in ruins

indicators.note: a ruin is a wreck whose parts lie scattered, so these letters must be rebuilt in a new order

blocks.note: the ten letters of these two words, taken as written

explanation.surface: A city like Rome left wrecked and in ruins.
explanation.definitionFit: A metropolis is a large and important urban centre, often a capital, so it is a big city.
